readerQuestion: How do I set up Music Assistant with Home Assistant, get one existing speaker playing, and choose the right player for a household routine?
directAnswer: Install the Music Assistant server using the HAOS app or supported standalone Docker route, configure one source and native player provider, and verify quiet one-room playback before adding the built-in Home Assistant integration. Use that integration's player in the kitchen radio script. Online sources still need internet and paid services retain their account requirements; synchronized groups require specific supported paths.
originalContribution: Section 5 provides a kitchen radio script walkthrough with an exact entity target, explicit queue replacement, account selection, a read-only station identifier lookup and a low-volume play/stop check. The six-row troubleshooting table separates source, discovery, audio-stream, integration, duplicate-control and grouping failures so the reader changes one layer at a time.
limitations: Documentation research only; no Home Assistant instance, speaker hardware, streaming account, audio delay, playback quality or synchronization was tested. The kitchen example is hypothetical and labeled accordingly. UI labels, authentication fields and provider support vary by installed version. Cast Sendspin bridging remains documented as experimental. The generated cover is an illustrative music-library scene, not hardware or installation evidence.

claimChecks.claim: The built-in Home Assistant integration requires an already running Music Assistant server and exposes MA players for controls and routines. HACS is not required.

The HA integration, reverse Home Assistant plugin in MA, and Home Assistant Media Players provider are different components. Most basic native-player setups only need the integration after the server is configured.

The documented installation routes are a HAOS app and a standalone Docker server; the latter needs persistent /data and appropriate direct network access. A supported 64-bit host and at least 2 GB RAM are required, with 4 GB+ recommended when sharing the host.
The current HAOS install path is Settings → Apps → App store; server start and opening its interface precede source and player setup.
HAOS sidebar ingress can initialize the administrator automatically; standalone first access has authentication setup. The guide does not prescribe deleting authentication data.

Home Assistant, MA and players must use the supported same-segment topology. Discovery announcements, Home Assistant control and player audio-stream access are distinct; an mDNS reflector or one open port does not establish all three. The guide notes same-segment exposure and offers a reversible test with one non-critical speaker.

The web interface normally uses TCP 8095; streaming starts on TCP 8097 and can move to a subsequent port if occupied. Other protocols retain their own requirements; the article does not present those two ports as a complete firewall rule set.

Prefer a native MA player provider when available. The generic HA Media Players fallback requires the Home Assistant plugin, filters for supported playback entities and does not promise synchronization with other types.
Radio Browser needs no login or subscription, and adding the provider alone does not populate the Radio view; select a station through Browse and add it to the library. This remains internet radio.
Spotify playback requires Premium. Playback-engine account restrictions and setup differences must be checked; the guide promises neither free-account playback nor offline streaming.
Local Files requires storage readable by MA; a laptop folder or an HA media path alone does not prove the MA container can access it.
When the integration requests MA login, the current project instructions require an admin account. Automations should target player entities belonging to the Music Assistant integration.

Play media supports the radio media type, enqueue choices including replace, precise media identifiers and explicit Username for scripts. Broad room/floor targets can include multiple media players, so the example selects one entity.

Get library items is read-only, selects the MA instance separately from entity targets, accepts radio/search/username options and returns item URIs. The station-name fallback is therefore a harmless lookup rather than a destructive repair.

Universal Groups play shared audio without synchronization; provider-supported sync groups differ. Sendspin bridges depend on devices/providers and Cast bridging is experimental. Active group ownership affects individual playback; members should not be deleted during playback.
Change one source or player at a time to narrow a fault; a working interface or moving progress display alone is not an audible playback verification.
